newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Lindsey submits resignation, effective Feb 5.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Lindsey submits resignation, effective Feb 5.

text.p: Lawrence Lindsey has submitted his resignation from the seven-member Federal Reserve Board of Governors, effective Feb. 5, the Fed said on Friday.
In his resignation letter to President Clinton, which was dated Thursday, Lindsey said he would not attend the Feb. 4 and 5 meeting of the Fed's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee.

The departure of Lindsey, an appointee of President George Bush, follows that of Fed Gov. Janet Yellen, who has been appointed chairman of the White House Council of Economic Advsiers. Yellen also will not attend the Feb 4 and 5 FOMC meeting.
In his resignation letter, Lindsey praised the Fed governors who whom he has worked since his appointment in 1991, especially Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan.
"The country has been fortunate to have had the services of each of them," Lindsey said.

"I therefore respectfully suggest that in your search for a successor to my seat on the board, that you consider my colleagues, past and present, as ideal role models for the type of individual who will be an asset to the board," Lindsey told the president.

Lindsey, 42, will join the American Enterprise Institute, a conservative Washington think tank, where he will become resident scholar and holder of the Arthur F. Burns Chair in Economics, the Fed said.

A former economics professor at Harvard University, Lindsey served on the White House Council of Economic Advisers under President Ronald Reagan for three years before joining the Bush administration and then becoming a Fed governor.

Lindsey called his tenure on the Fed "one of the most personally and intellectually enriching experiences of my life" and said the monetary policy it has shaped "has made our economic performance the envy of the world."
